drafted_from: tool row in tools/benchmark-small-local-models/tool-rows.json, do-work/time_a_decider.py and test/test_benchmark.py (Decider)
start_here: Say to your AI: "Time how long the decider someone/decider-small takes to load and to answer on my computer, and how much memory it holds."

lists.label: Settings
lists.holds: One row per tool and scope (a person, a film, a piece or the whole account): the settings that tool reads when it runs, as JSON.

instructions: 1. Pour the two example settings rows into your own list:settings (see pour), or write your own row record:setting:benchmark-small-local-models~person~<you> whose settings hold {"commands":{"time_a_decider":{...your defaults}}}.
2. Say the line in start_here. Your AI reads this tool's row with tools:list {tool: "tool:time-a-small-local-decider"} and gets its run command.

3. Your AI writes the request as a JSON file (request.json), adds settings_record from your settings row if you keep one, and runs python3 trillion-workshop/tools/benchmark-small-local-models/do-work/time_a_decider.py request.json on your computer.
4. It reads the last line the script prints: {"result": ...} or {"error": "what to change"} (exit code 2), then tells you the result in plain words.
5. Tell the person the load seconds, the milliseconds per answer (the case is asked four times) and the memory. A model not in the Hugging Face cache is refused with the command to fetch it.

worked_examples.title: A decider timed over four answers on the cpu
worked_examples.ask: How fast does this small decider run on my computer?
worked_examples.given: From tools/benchmark-small-local-models/test/test_benchmark.py (Decider.test_a_decider_is_timed), run with the test's stand-in decider snapshot. request.json = {"model":"someone/decider-small","revision":"abc","device":"cpu"}. Run: python3 trillion-workshop/tools/benchmark-small-local-models/do-work/time_a_decider.py request.json
worked_examples.hands_back: {"result":{"device":"cpu","load_s":0.0,"ms":[0,0,0,0],"choice":"billing","confidence":0.333,"alloc_GB":0.0,"maxrss_GB":0.01}}: four timed answers (ms list of 4), the made-up two-question case answered "billing" with 0.333. With {"model":"someone/absent"} the last line is {"error":"someone/absent is not in this computer's model cache (...); download it there (hf download someone/absent) or set HF_HUB_CACHE"} and the exit code is 2.

pour.how: Name the list you already keep for the same job and read it with records:read (its fields and row type). Run tool:pour-example-rows-into-my-list with that list as into and this kit list as kit_list: it matches each kit field to one of yours (your map, the same id, the same label, or a name in alike), pours nothing under 80% and names the fields with no home, and otherwise answers the one records:write that adds the example rows beside your own.
